title: Ambiguous Password Spraying Pattern During Contractor Onboarding
description: Several accounts received one or two failed sign-in attempts from a single external IP. A newly onboarded contractor then successfully logged in from the same IP, but the source is not listed as an approved corporate or contractor network.
raw_logs: 2026-07-02T17:10:00Z identity_provider src_ip=203.0.113.240 targeted_users=33 failures=45 window_minutes=27 error=invalid_password
2026-07-02T17:31:18Z identity_provider user=temp.vendor@company.example src_ip=203.0.113.240 login_result=success device_id=unknown mfa_result=success
alert_source: Identity Provider, HR System, Network Inventory
remediation: Temporarily restrict the contractor account pending verification, contact the account sponsor through a trusted channel, review post-login activity, investigate all targeted accounts, and block or challenge the source if it cannot be validated.
analyst_notes: The pattern resembles password spraying, but the successful account belongs to a legitimate new contractor and completed MFA. The unapproved source IP and broad failed attempts remain concerning, so this requires containment and verification rather than an immediate assumption of benign activity.
expected_answer: This is an uncertain but likely malicious password-spraying scenario. The model should map it to T1110.003, assign high severity because a successful login followed broad failed attempts, explain the contradictory onboarding evidence, and request identity verification plus post-login review.
